results.title: Baseten Billing and Cost Control: An Evaluation (2026) — andrew.ooo
results.author: Andrew
highlights:
Published: October 19, 2026 

## The short answer

Baseten bills each running replica by the minute, including the minutes it spends cold-starting, and its budget feature does not stop dedicated deployments. Cost control therefore lives in your autoscaling settings — `min_replica`, `max_replica` and `scale_down_delay` — not in the billing dashboard. Done well, a spiky workload costs a fraction of an always-on replica; done badly, a forgotten warm H100 costs about $4,680 a month. Facts below are from Baseten’s documentation, read October 19, 2026.

## What you pay per minute

| Instance | Per minute | Per hour (×60) | GPU memory |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| L4 (`L4:4x16`) | $0.01414 | ~$0.85 | 24 GiB |
| A100 (`A100:12x144`) | $0.06667 | ~$4.00 | 80 GiB |
| H100 | $0.10833 | ~$6.50 | 80 GiB |
| H200 | $0.12500 | $7.50 | 141 GiB |
| B200 | $0.16633 | ~$9.98 | 180 GiB |
| 8× H100 (`H100:8`) | $0.86664 | ~$52.00 | 640 GiB |

The Basic plan is $0 a month, pay as you go, with starting credits for new workspaces; there is no perpetual free tier. If credits run out and no payment method is on file, Baseten deactivates your models.

Baseten’s instance reference lists one on-demand price per instance — H100 $0.10833/minute (about $6.50/hour), H200 $0.125 ($7.50), B200 $0.16633 (about $9.98), A100 $0.06667 (about $4.00) — and no spot or preemptible tier. results.title: Baseten Pricing Compared to Other ML Infrastructure Tools — andrew.ooo
results.author: Andrew
highlights:
Published: November 4, 2026 • Updated: November 5, 2026 

## The short answer

Baseten charges more per GPU-hour than Modal, Replicate or RunPod, and it is the one you pick for managed, optimized production serving, not for the cheapest raw GPU. On November 4, 2026 a single H100 lists at about $6.50/hour on Baseten, $5.49 on Replicate, $3.99 on a RunPod Secure Cloud pod and $3.95 on Modal. Pick:

- Baseten — custom or fine-tuned models in production where latency and reliability matter more than GPU price.
- Modal — Python teams with spiky or batch workloads; per-second billing and the lowest serverless H100 rate.
- RunPod — the lowest raw GPU price (Community Cloud), if you can run your own serving stack.
- Replicate — public models priced per output (images, video) and quick demos.

This page is a spoke of our Baseten evaluation; for how Baseten’s minute meter behaves, see Baseten billing and cost control.

## GPU prices side by side (November 4, 2026)

| GPU | Baseten (per min → per hr) | Modal (per sec → per hr) | Replicate | RunPod pod (Secure / Community) | RunPod Serverless |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| H100 80GB | $0.10833 → ~$6.50 | $0.001097 → ~$3.95 | $0.001525/s → $5.49 | $3.99 / $2.69 | $5.39 |
| H200 141GB | $0.125 → $7.50 | $0.001261 → ~$4.54 | — | $5.29 / $3.59 | $6.99 |
| B200 180GB | $0.16633 → ~$9.98 | $0.001736 → ~$6.25 | — | $7.99 / $5.98 | $10.79 |
| A100 80GB | $0.06667 → ~$4.00 | $0.000694 → ~$2.50 | $5.04 | $1.79 / $1.39 (SXM) | $2.72 |
| RTX PRO 6000 96GB | $0.06667 → ~$4.00 | $0.000842 → ~$3.03 | — | $2.49 (Secure) | $3.49 |
| Billing unit | Per minute, per replica | Per second | Per second | Per second / hour | Per second |

Baseten rates are from its instance-type reference, Modal’s from its pricing page, Replicate’s from its hardware price list and RunPod’s from its pricing page (updated November 4, 2026). Hourly figures for Baseten and Modal are our conversion.

Hardware is not identical: a Baseten `H100` instance includes 16 vCPUs and 118 GiB of RAM, and RunPod’s SXM and PCIe H100s are priced separately ($3.99 SXM, $2.89 PCIe on Secure Cloud). Compare the instance that actually fits your model.

## Pricing disclaimer

Prices are list prices in US dollars read on each vendor’s pages and docs on 13 October 2026, before tax, volume discounts or promotions unless stated. Self-hosting figures cover GPU compute only. We didn’t generate, render or measure anything; quality and speed figures are from the independent leaderboards named or labelled as vendor claims. Prices and terms change often, so confirm with the vendor before you commit. Dbggr isn’t affiliated with any vendor here.

# Baseten Evaluation 2026: Pricing, Strengths, Alternatives

 Published: October 9, 2026 • Updated: November 4, 2026 

## What changed as of November 2026

- A bigger round is reported, not announced. Bloomberg reported on October 30, 2026 that Baseten is set to raise about $2B in two tranches priced at $26B and $30B. Until Baseten announces it, the confirmed figure remains the $13B June 2026 Series F.
- OpenAI partnership (September 29, 2026): OpenAI enterprise customers can use open models served by Baseten inside Codex and the Responses API.
- Prices re-checked November 3, 2026, unchanged: H100 $0.10833/min, B200 $0.16633/min, A100 $0.06667/min, L4 $0.01414/min; DeepSeek V4.1 Flash $0.30 / $0.007 / $1.20 per MTok (Baseten’s hosted rate; DeepSeek’s own API charges $0.15 / $0.60 off-peak and $0.30 / $1.20 at peak). Together’s dedicated H100 ($5.49/h) and B200 ($8.99/h) are also unchanged.

...

## Pricing

| Item | Baseten list price | For comparison |
| --- | --- | --- |
| H100 (dedicated) | $0.10833/min ≈ $6.50/h | Together AI dedicated H100 $5.49/h on demand |
| B200 (dedicated) | $0.16633/min ≈ $9.98/h | Together AI dedicated B200 $8.99/h |
| A100 80GB | $0.06667/min ≈ $4.00/h | — |
| L4 | $0.01414/min ≈ $0.85/h | — |
| DeepSeek V4.1 Flash Model API | $0.30 / $0.007 cached / $1.20 per MTok | Fireworks and Together $0.30 / $0.006 / $1.20 |
| Plans | Pay as you go (no contract); production-scale capacity and custom pricing via sales | — |

Baseten bills by the minute per replica, including the minutes a replica spends deploying and scaling up. Aggressive scale-to-zero on a large model can therefore cost more than one warm replica.

...

## Weaknesses

1. Price per GPU-hour is above GPU clouds and about 18% above Together’s on-demand H100.
2. Model API catalog is narrower than Fireworks or Together — fine for DeepSeek, Kimi K3 and GLM 5.3, thin beyond.
3. Pro access to scarce GPUs is a paid tier; Basic customers compete for capacity.

results.title: Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16 | GPUJournal
highlights:
# Lambda announces GPU price rises of about 15% — B200, H100 and A100 80GB, from Nov 16

Nov 6, 2026

Read on Lambda's own pricing page today, Nov 6, 2026: the Instances table now prints the prices that take effect on Nov 16, 2026 — HGX B200 up $1.00 an hour, H100 up $0.60 and A100 80GB up $0.40. It is the largest single announced rise we have caught this autumn, and renters have ten days' notice.

Image: GPUJournal price record — read on lambda.ai/pricing

What was announced, in the pricing page's own words (read Nov 6, 2026): 'These prices take effect November 16, 2026, at 00:00 UTC. Until then, log in to your Lambda Cloud account to see current pricing.' The printed Nov 16 rates: HGX B200 $7.69 an hour (from the $6.69 last verified on Nov 5, +14.9%), HGX H100 $4.59 (from $3.99, +15.0%), HGX A100 80GB $3.19 (from $2.79, +14.3%), and HGX A100 40GB unchanged at $1.99. Lambda is also now at a new address — lambda.com — announced on its blog on Nov 5, 2026; the pricing page itself still answers at lambda.ai/pricing.

How we are treating it: an announced rise is not a live price. Our board keeps Lambda's last verified rates until Nov 16 and will move only when the new rates are re-verified in effect on or after that date — the rise is recorded in Price Watch today as announced, with both dates. One consequence of the announcement is already live, though: Lambda's currently-effective rates can no longer be read on its public page, only after logging in, so today's public check could verify the future rates but not re-read the current ones.

What it does to the board when it lands: Lambda's B200 at $6.69 is currently the cheapest verified HGX B200 instance rate we list from a self-serve cloud; at $7.69 it would sit above RunPod Community's $5.98 marketplace rate and just below RunPod Secure's $7.99. Its H100 at $4.59 would remain above the board's best H100 SXM offer (TensorDock, from $2.25 at an 8-GPU minimum) but move Lambda from the middle of the H100 pack toward its top. Around-the-clock, the announced rises add about $730 a month per B200, $438 per H100 and $292 per A100 80GB on a 730-hour month.

results.title: The H100 got more expensive · Three Phase. Potentia Intelligence.
results.author: Jose Mir
highlights:
### One Big Thing · Phase 3 · Compute

What happened: Nebius raised on-demand GPU prices on October 1, its second hike in about three months. Independent trackers show the same direction across the market.

Why it matters: The bear case on AI infrastructure assumed GPUs lose value fast. Rental rates are the cleanest test of that assumption, and so far the test is failing.

By the numbers:

- Nebius list price for an H100 went from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour; B300 from $7.85 to $9.50.
- The Ornn H100 index settled at $3.17 on October 23, up about 4% in a month.
